title: WPSS/4081/2018 of MIRAJ ALI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 4081 (S/S) of 2018
Miraj Ali .....Petitioner
Versus
Sate of Uttarakhand
Through its Secretary Drinking Water Department,
Government of Uttarakhand and others ....Respondents
Ms. Rajni Supyal, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. B.S. Bist, Advocate on behalf of Mr. D.S. Patni, Advocate for the respondent.

Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 The petitioner has superannuated from the service of
the respondents from the post of Daftry. After his retirement, he
has claimed for the post retiral dues and the same stood sanctioned
by the respondents by the order dated 1st February, 2018 and 3rd
February, 2018.
2. The contention of the learned counsel for the
petitioner is that despite of the sanction being granted, when the
retiral dues were not paid, the petitioner has submitted several
representations before the authority concerned but still the
grievance of the petitioner remained un-addressed, which resulted
into filing of the present Writ petition. In para 9 of the writ
petition, it has been stated that despite of the fact that leave
encashment and gratuity have already stood sanctioned by the
respondent by the order dated 1st February, 2018 and 3rd February,
2018, but the same has not been paid. Details of post retiral dues
read as under :
"1 Leave encashment of 300 days (sanctioned
vide order dated 3.2.2018 but not paid)
Rs.3,18,943/-
2 Gratuity (calculated and sanctioned to pay
vide order dated 10.05.2018 but not paid )
Rs.6,21,968/-
3 Arrears of salary difference of 7th Pay Scale
for which the petitioner is legally entitled
and admitted to the respondent but not paid
Rs.26,760/-
 Total Rs. 9,67,671/-"

2
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that
similarly, arrears of 7th Pay Commission too has also been
admitted by the respondent, but the same could not be paid.
4. For the aforesaid reliefs, the petitioner claims parity
based on the judgment rendered in an identical Writ Petition, being
Writ Petition No. 1576 of 2018 (S/S), Govind Ballabh Pandey
Vs. Uttarakhand Payjal Sansadhan Vikas Evam Nirman
Nigam as decided by this Court on 14.06.2018.
5. As such, a writ of mandamus is issued to the
respondent Nigam directing him to pay the post retiral dues as
explained in para 10 of the writ petition for the following heads :
"1 Leave encashment of 300 days
(sanctioned vide order dated 3.2.2018
but not paid) (within three months)
Rs.3,18,943/-
2 Gratuity (calculated and sanctioned to
pay vide order dated 10.05.2018 but not
paid ) (in two months)
Rs.6,21,968/-
 Total Rs. 9,40,911
6. The respondents/Nigam is directed to pay the post
retiral dues to the petitioner as mentioned in paragraph No. 5 of the
judgment within a period as mentioned against each head of dues
payable to the petitioner from the date of presentation of the
certified copy of the judgment.
7. As far as relief prayed for the payment of arrears of 7th
Pay Commission is concerned, though this Court has earlier passed
the order for paying arrears of 7th Pay Commission within one
month, but the learned counsel for the respondent has placed
before this Court the judgment rendered by the Division Bench in
Writ Petition No. 530 (SB) of 2018, Munna Lal Gupta Vs. State
of Uttarakhand and others as decided on 20th November, 2018,
whereby, the Division Bench has held that since the issue

3
pertaining to the payment of arrears of 7th Pay Commission is
pending consideration before the State Government, the State
Government would take a decision on the same as expeditiously as
possible and communicate the decision so taken to the
Corporation and as soon as the decision is taken, the Corporation
would make the payment of arrears of 7th Pay Commission to the
petitioner as claimed by him.
8. Subject to the above observations, the writ petition
stands disposed of.
9. However, there would be no order as to costs.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 07.12.2018
Shiv
